Based on the standard node2vec method (Grover & Leskovec, 2016), the usual three phases are: (1) Compute transition probabilities: for each edge, set a second-order biased transition probability, using return parameter p and in-out parameter q, so the walk can interpolate between BFS-like and DFS-like exploration. (2) Generate random walks: from each node, run a fixed number of biased random walks of a set length, repeated over many iterations, to produce a corpus of node sequences. (3) Learn embeddings: feed the walks to a skip-gram model (word2vec-style, typically with negative sampling, optimized by stochastic gradient descent) so that nodes co-occurring in walks get similar vectors. If the passage describes the phases differently, its description should take precedence.
